title: What time is it? (Wie spät ist es?)
summary: Ask and tell the time two ways: the official way (14:30, vierzehn Uhr dreißig) and the everyday way (halb drei). Say when something happens: um neun Uhr.
goals: Ask what time it is and answer
Say times the official way, as on timetables and at work
Say times the everyday way: Viertel nach, halb, Viertel vor
Say when something happens: um drei Uhr

sections.title: Two ways to tell the time
sections.text:
To ask: [[Wie spät ist es?]] or [[Wie viel Uhr ist es?]] Both mean 'What time is it?'. The answer starts with [[Es ist ...]]: [[Es ist drei Uhr.]]

German has two ways to say a time:
- **Official:** the 24-hour clock, read like the numbers on a screen: 14:30 = [[vierzehn Uhr dreißig]]. You hear it on timetables, at work, on the radio and for appointments.
- **Everyday:** the 12-hour clock with [[nach]], [[vor]], [[Viertel]] and [[halb]]: 14:30 = [[halb drei]]. Friends and colleagues talk like this.

You need to understand both. When you speak, either is fine.

sections.title: The official way: hours, Uhr, minutes
The trap: halb
sections.text:
[[halb vier]] is **3:30**, not 4:30. German counts the half hour *towards* the next hour: halfway to four.

So [[halb neun]] = 8:30, [[halb zwölf]] = 11:30, [[halb eins]] = 12:30. Every time: halb + the **next** hour.

The everyday way uses only 1 to 12. 15:00 is just [[drei]] or [[drei Uhr]]; the situation tells you which three.

sections.title: Think in Russian here
sections.text:
Russian counts like German: половина четвёртого is 3:30, 'half of the fourth hour', just like [[halb vier]].

Armenian and English count from the hour that has passed: երեքն անց կես and 'half past three' are 3:30 too, but they name the three. Translate from them and you'll say [[halb drei]], which is 2:30: a full hour too early.

And Russian час and Armenian ժամ mean both 'hour' and 'o'clock'. German has two words: [[drei Uhr]] is a point on the clock, [[drei Stunden]] is how long something takes.

sections.title: In Munich you'll also hear ...
sections.text: In Bavaria and in the east of Germany, many people say [[viertel vier]] for 3:15 (a quarter of the way to four) and [[dreiviertel vier]] for 3:45 (three quarters of the way). It's the logic of [[halb]], and of Russian четверть четвёртого (3:15). You don't need to say these yourself; just recognise them when a colleague says [[Der Kurs ist um viertel vier.]]

sections.title: At what time? um
sections.text:
To say *when* something happens, use [[um]] + the time: [[Der Kurs ist um neun Uhr.]]

To ask: [[Wann?]] or [[Um wie viel Uhr?]]
- [[Wann ist der Kurs?]] - [[Um halb zehn.]]
- [[Um wie viel Uhr kommst du?]] - [[Um acht.]]

Compare: [[Wie spät ist es?]] asks for the time now; [[Wann?]] asks when something happens.

items.de: Wie spät ist es? - Es ist zehn nach acht.
items.en: What time is it? - It's ten past eight.

items.de: Es ist jetzt Viertel vor zwölf.
Der Kurs ist um halb zehn.
items.en: The class is at half past nine.

items.note: Stunden = how long; Uhr = a time on the clock

items.question: Which one is 3:30?
items.explanation: halb + the next hour: halfway to four = 3:30. The official way, drei Uhr dreißig, would be right too.

items.question: Which one is 8:45?
items.explanation: 8:45 is a quarter before nine: Viertel vor neun.

items.instruction: Write the time the everyday way: 7:10.
items.explanation: 10 minutes after seven: zehn nach sieben.

items.audio: Der Kurs ist um halb zehn.
items.question: When is the class?

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: What time is it?
items.explanation: Wie spät ist es? Literally: how late is it? You can also ask: Wie viel Uhr ist es?
